dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the canary target track the same environment id the producer publishes (e.g. derive from REBAR_ENV_ID/vars) rather than hardcoding `--target reconciler`.
evidence: scripts/canary_bridge.py:169: "--target", / "reconciler",
src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/last_pass.py:329: environment_id=os.environ.get("REBAR_ENV_ID"),
last_pass.resolve_environment_id falls back to `local:<.env-id>` when REBAR_ENV_ID is unset (last_pass.py:77-84)
.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:249: REBAR_ENV_ID: ${{ vars.REBAR_ENV_ID || 'reconciler' }}
dropped.finding: The status canary always invokes `rebar bridge status --target reconciler`, but the reconciler producer publishes the last-pass record with `environment_id=os.environ.get("REBAR_ENV_ID")` (falling back to `local:<.env-id>`). The producer workflow sets `REBAR_ENV_ID: ${{ vars.REBAR_ENV_ID || 'reconciler' }}`, so any deployment overriding `vars.REBAR_ENV_ID` to a non-`reconciler` value causes the canary target to mismatch the recorded producer id, yielding a FOREIGN verdict and a false stale alarm even for a healthy successful pass.
scenarios: A project sets repository variable REBAR_ENV_ID to a custom id; producer records it, canary keeps comparing against literal 'reconciler' → FOREIGN → false-alarm bug filed every run.
